record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
record.original_question: Let F = {a1, ..., aℓ} be Hardy-field functions of polynomial growth such that every nontrivial linear combination a in span*(F) stays farther than O(log t) from every real multiple of every integer polynomial. For every ergodic system (X, B, μ, T) and bounded measurable f1, ..., fℓ, must the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T^{[a1(n)]}f1 · ... · T^{[aℓ(n)]}fℓ converge in L^2 to (∫ f1 dμ) · ... · (∫ fℓ dμ)?

evidence.quote: Problem 23. Let F be as above and suppose that for every function a ∈ span∗(F) we have |a(t) − cp(t)|/ log t → ∞ for every c ∈ R and p ∈ Z[t]. Show that for every ergodic system (X, B, µ, T) and functions f1, . . . , f` ∈ L∞(µ) we have limN→∞ (1/N) ΣN n=1 T^[a1(n)]f1 · · · T^[a`(n)]f` = ∫ f1 dµ · · · ∫ f` dµ where the convergence takes place in L^2(µ).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ denote a Hardy field, i.e., a field of germs at $+\infty$ of real-valued functions defined on a half-line $[c,\infty)$ that is closed under differentiation. A function $a \in \mathcal{H}$ is said to have polynomial growth if there exists $k \in \mathbb{N}$ with $a(t)/t^k \to 0$ as $t \to \infty$. 

Let $F = \{a_1, \dots, a_\ell\} \subset \mathcal{H}$ be functions of polynomial growth, and let $\operatorname{span}_*(F)$ denote the set of all nontrivial real-linear combinations $c_1 a_1 + \cdots + c_\ell a_\ell$ with $(c_1,\dots,c_\ell) \in \mathbb{R}^\ell \setminus \{0\}$. Suppose that for every $a \in \operatorname{span}_*(F)$, every $c \in \mathbb{R}$, and every polynomial $p \in \mathbb{Z}[t]$,
$$\frac{|a(t) - c\, p(t)|}{\log t} \longrightarrow \infty \quad \text{as } t \to \infty.$$

Let $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$ be an ergodic invertible measure-preserving system on a standard probability space, and let $f_1, \dots, f_\ell \in L^\infty(\mu)$. Prove or disprove that
$$\lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{1}{N} \sum_{n=1}^{N} T^{\lfloor a_1(n) \rfloor} f_1 \cdot T^{\lfloor a_2(n) \rfloor} f_2 \cdots T^{\lfloor a_\ell(n) \rfloor} f_\ell \;=\; \prod_{i=1}^{\ell} \int f_i\, d\mu$$
with convergence in $L^2(\mu)$.
artifact.category_tag: Multiple ergodic averages along Hardy sequences
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (joint ergodicity for Hardy-field tuples whose nontrivial linear combinations stay super-logarithmically far from real multiples of integer polynomials) has been established. Tsinas (arXiv:2109.07941, "Joint ergodicity of Hardy field sequences") proves the L^2 convergence to the product of integrals under exactly this log-t separation hypothesis, explicitly confirming Frantzikinakis's conjecture. Subsequent works (e.g., Frantzikinakis–Kuca and later papers on resolving the joint ergodicity problem for Hardy sequences) extend and reaffirm the result.

status_evidence.title: Joint ergodicity of Hardy field sequences
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes a conjecture of Frantzikinakis: if all non-trivial linear combinations stay logarithmically away from rational polynomials, then the L^2-limit equals the product of the integrals in ergodic systems.
status_evidence.claim: The Hardy-field joint ergodicity conjecture under the log-t separation hypothesis is proved.

status_evidence.title: Resolving the joint ergodicity problem for Hardy sequences
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work essentially resolves the joint ergodicity problem for polynomial and Hardy sequences of polynomial growth.
status_evidence.claim: Follow-up work has resolved the joint ergodicity problem for Hardy sequences.

status_evidence.title: Joint ergodicity for functions of polynomial growth
status_evidence.snippet: Confirms conjectures posed by Frantzikinakis and gives combinatorial applications.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is confirmed in published form.
